ruling.recommended_action: Close the fare dispute with no refund: the off-route segment of 14:21–14:30 is the route to the rider's own named Clementi Mall stop, exempt under RD-3(a); the $1.04 metered waiting unit is chargeable under RD-3(c). No account flag (relies on RD-6, which requires a non-exempt segment or a recorded RD-1 breach).

segment_findings.reason: RD-3(a): the rider named the place — 'Can you stop at Clementi Mall' [F9] — and the driver agreed before the segment began [F10]; the car stopped there for 4 min 0 s at 14:23–14:27, inside the 14:21–14:30 off-route window [F2][F4]. A rider-named stop is not a detour, so the whole 1.70 km extra driven to reach it is exempt and its extra km are not refundable [RD-3(a)][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The +2.0 km / +23% actual-vs-optimal gap [F1] does not by itself create a refund: the trace shows a single off-route segment [F4], and that segment is exempt because it is the route to the rider's named Clementi Mall stop [F9][F10][F2][RD-3(a)]. The $14.88 distance line is the metered charge for kilometres to the rider's own requested stop [F8][RD-2].

Correct on the segment's dimensions (3.80 km vs 2.10 km optimal, +1.70 km, up to 555 m off route) [F4], but RD-1 does not make every off-route segment chargeable — the segment is reviewed under RD-3 and is exempt there [F9][F10][F2][RD-3(a)].
This claim is accepted: the stop was rider-named [F9] and agreed [F10], matching the recorded stationary period [F2]. It is therefore the basis for exemption, not for a refund [RD-3(a)].

The premise that the stop explains only a small part of the 3.80 km segment [F4] does not survive RD-3(a): the segment is the route to the named stop, and the rule exempts the whole segment driven to reach it, so no residual unexempted kilometres remain for RD-1 to catch [F9][F10][F2][RD-3(a)][RD-2].

Correct as to RD-4 — no qualifying incident [F14] and bands 4/5 do not exempt [F12][F13] — but RD-4 is not the operative exemption here; the segment is already exempt under RD-3(a), so the absence of traffic cause is immaterial [RD-3][RD-4].

The arithmetic 1.70 km × $1.41/km = $2.40 [F4][F8] is right, but it applies only to non-exempt segments; this segment is exempt under RD-3(a), so the RD-2 refundable amount is 0 and no_action follows [RD-2][RD-3].
Accepted by both sides: the $1.04 metered waiting unit for the 4-minute rider-requested stop [F2][F6] is chargeable on RydeTAXI and is not refunded [RD-3(c)].

RD-6 requires a finding against the driver in this case (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach) before the history counts [F17]; no such finding exists because the segment is exempt [F4][F9][F10][RD-3(a)][RD-6]. The 90-day profile alone cannot create it [F16][F17].

The driver's conclusion (no refund) is right, but the reason given — that RD-2 is satisfied by the mere fact that the stop was named — is imprecise; the exemption comes from RD-3(a) because the rider named the place and the car stopped there [F2][F4][F9][F10][RD-3(a)][RD-2], not from RD-2 itself.

Accepted as to outcome, but as framed it is circular: RD-6's precondition is measured by the RD-2 refund or a recorded RD-1 breach [F4][RD-2][RD-6], not by the driver's own assertion that no violation exists; it is RD-3(a) that removes the breach here [F9][F10][F2][RD-3(a)].
